ORAL JUDGMENT Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and award dated 16th August, 2016 passed in Motor Accident Claims Petition No.543 of 1997 by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.),
Surat, the original claimants have preferred this First Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act for enhancement of compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/783/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined 1.1

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Petition No.543 of 1997
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The original claim of the claimants was for Rs.06,80,000/-.
As against that, the learned Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.03,90,800/- under various heads as under.

Particulars Amount (in Rs.)
Future Loss of Income 02,80,800/-
Funeral charges 10,000/-
Loss of consortium & love and 01,00,000/-
affection Total 03,90,800/-
2.
It is the case of the claimants that on 22nd October, 1996 the deceased was travelling in Truck bearing Registration No.GJ-7X-499.
The driver of the said Truck was driving the Truck in rash and negligent manner and thereby lost his control over the vehicle and resultantly accident took place.
Pursuant to the said accident, the deceased received severe injuries and was hospitalised, where ultimately he succumbed to those injuries.

2.1 The claimants being heirs and legal representatives of the deceased, approached the learned Tribunal for compensation for untimely death of the deceased by way of application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
3. The learned Tribunal, after having considered the materials produced on record, held the driver of the Truck as sole responsible for the accident in question.
3.1 The Tribunal thereafter proceeded to award NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/783/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined compensation by computing the income of the deceased at Rs.01,500/- per month.
The learned Tribunal has also considered prospective income rise at 30%.
Thus, the actual income came to be assessed at Rs.23,400/- (Rs.1500/- X 12 X 30%).
The learned Tribunal, having considered family members, deducted one-fifth amount towards the personal expenditure.
Having considered the age of 38 years, the learned Tribunal adopted multiplier of 15 and thus, the Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.02,80,800/- towards future loss of income.
The learned Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head of funeral expenses, Rs.01,00,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

Thus, in all, the learned Tribunal awarded sum of Rs.03,90,800/-
with 9% interest.
4. Feeling aggrieved by the aforesaid, claimants have approached this Court by way of this Appeal seeking enhancement in the compensation.

I have heard learned advocate Mr.Hiren Modi for the appellants - claimants and learned advocate Ms.Niyati Juthani for the respondent - insurance company.
6. Learned advocate the appellants - claimants submitted that the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is on a very lower side and thereby cannot be said to be adequate in nature.

Learned advocate has placed heavy reliance on the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company limited v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680], Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2006) 9 SCC 121], The New India NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/783/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined Assurance Company Limited v. Smt.Somwati [(2020)
9 SCC 644] and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram & Ors.

sentences.text: and submitted that this Court may appropriately enhance the award by considering the aforesaid judgments.
7. Per contra, learned advocate Ms.Juthani for the insurance company vehemently opposed the appeal on all available counts, however could not dispute the law laid down by the Apex Court.
7.1 By making aforesaid submissions, requested this Court to pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.
8. I have heard learned advocates for the respective parties and have gone through the record and proceedings of the Tribunal concerned.
No other and/or further submissions have been advanced by the respective advocates except what are stated hereinabove.

9. Considering the submissions of rival parties and having considered the materials produced on record, short question that falls for consideration is whether the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal can be said to be adequate in nature?
10. So as to decide the aforesaid question, it would be apt to consider catena of decisions passed by the Apex Court whereby the law of adequate compensation is settled.

Considering the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and keeping in mind the age at 38 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/783/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined years of the deceased,
prospective income is required to be considered at the rate of 40%.
As the learned advocate appearing for the appellants has not much disputed about income at Rs.01,500/- per month, I propose to add 40% thereon towards the future rise in income.
Considering the number of dependents, one-fifth amount is required to be deducted towards personal expenditure.
Keeping in mind the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra), multiplier of 15 is proposed to be adopted.
Keeping in mind the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), all the dependents are eligible for compensation under the head of loss of consortium at Rs.40,000/- each.
I answer the question accordingly.
11. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal requires to be modified as under.
Particulars Amount (in Rs.)

Loss of dependency 03,02,400/-

 Rs.600/- (40% future  prospectus)

X 12 - Rs.5040/-
 (1/5 personal expenditure) X 15  X 18 (multiplier)
Funeral & transport expenses 15,000/-
Loss of estate 15,000/-
Consortium 03,20,000/-
(Rs.40000/- X 8)

Total 06,52,400/-
Amount already awarded 03,90,800/-
Additional amount to be paid 02,61,600/-
 NEUTRAL  C/FA/783/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/01/2023  undefin 12.
Resultantly, the appeal is partly allowed.
The appellants - claimants shall be entitled to amount of Rs.02,61,600/- by way of additional compensation, to be paid with 6% interest, from the date of application till its realisation.

The insurance company is directed to deposit Rs.02,61,600/- with proportionate costs and interest before the learned Tribunal within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
13.
The Tribunal shall issue Account Payee cheque in the name of the claimants after identification and proper verification.
Record & Proceedings, if any, to be sent back.
